title: Manual Updates vs Immer
definition: Comparing the legacy way of writing immutable spread operations against the modern Immer mutating syntax to understand why RTK is the standard.
simpleExplanation: A side-by-side comparison. Writing manual immutable updates for nested data feels like doing advanced algebra. Immer feels like writing plain, simple JavaScript.
realWorldExample: Updating a user's address. `return { ...state, user: { ...state.user, address: { ...state.user.address, city: 'NY' } } }` vs `state.user.address.city = 'NY'`.

basic: Which approach takes more lines of code: Manual or Immer?
intermediate: Is there any performance penalty for using Immer instead of manual spread operators?

answers.question: Which takes more?
answers.answer: Manual updates take vastly more lines of code and are highly prone to syntax errors (missing brackets).

answers.question: Performance penalty?
answers.answer: Technically, yes. Immer uses Proxies which take a few milliseconds of processing time. However, in 99.9% of web apps, this difference is completely unnoticeable, and the developer experience gained is absolutely worth it.
